title: Server keys
inventoryDesc: Read-only key inventory. Back up file-based keys and database-backed federation identities separately. Secret material is never displayed. Push credentials are listed under Push.
channelDesc: Valid configuration does not guarantee delivery. Send a test from the push devices page.
directoryHelp: Directory precedence: SOMS_CONFIG_DIR → SOMS_DATA_DIR → data under the process working directory. These are the actual or expected server-side paths. In containers, they are container paths; mount the corresponding directory on persistent storage.
restart: Files are loaded at startup. Restart the server after adding or replacing them.
managed: Automatically generated on first startup. Persist and back up this file; do not casually delete or replace it.
fcmPlacement: Download the service account private-key JSON from Firebase, name it firebase-service-account.json, and place it at the path below. This is the server send credential, not google-services.json. Restrict file permissions.
clientPlacement: Download google-services.json for the Android app from Firebase and place it at the path below. It initializes the client and must belong to the same Firebase project as the server credential.
runtimeHelp: Credential cards describe the current files. Send channel status indicates initialization at startup, not successful remote authentication or delivery.
fingerprintHelp: Identifies whether a key has changed without revealing the key itself. It does not prove delivery; fingerprints from different entries are not comparable.
healthHelp: Validates VAPID keys and contact subject locally. No network delivery is performed.

federation-root.name: Federation root key
federation-root.help: The trust root for the federation identity, used to certify signing keys. Stored in the database, not a file. Losing it breaks existing trust; rotate through supported federation identity workflows, never by editing database rows.

federation-signing.name: Federation signing key
federation-signing.help: Signs server-to-server federation requests and is certified by the root key. Stored in the database and managed by the federation key lifecycle; do not replace it manually.

vapid.name: Web Push VAPID
vapid.help: Authenticates this server to browser push services. The public key may be shared with clients; the private key must remain secret. Replacing the key may invalidate existing browser subscriptions and require resubscription.

admin-jwt.name: Admin JWT key
admin-jwt.help: Signs and verifies administration authentication tokens. Replacing it invalidates existing admin tokens and requires signing in again.

password-pepper.name: Password pepper
password-pepper.help: Participates in Argon2 hashing for user and admin passwords, mitigating offline attacks after a database-only leak. Losing or replacing it prevents verification of existing passwords and requires password resets.

two-factor.name: Two-factor encryption key
two-factor.help: Protects admin TOTP secrets and recovery codes. Losing or replacing it makes existing two-factor data unusable and requires a controlled recovery and re-enrollment process.

firebase-service-account.name: FCM server send credential
firebase-service-account.help: The server uses a Firebase service account to send FCM pushes to Android devices. It is not Android client configuration; never expose its private key. Revoked or invalid credentials prevent sending.
